provenance: MW Sprint Performance System strength prescriptions. Weeks 9-41 are synchronized constructed prescriptions; do not represent as recovered historical workouts.

1.title: WEEK 1 - FOUNDATION ENTRY
1.coachNote: Rest 20-30 sec between circuit exercises and 60-90 sec between rounds. Learn positions; no grinding reps. Track-first adjustment: Complete high-intensity sprint work before lifting. If the athlete is unusually fatigued, remove the final circuit round or accessory block before reducing the quality of the primary sprint session.

2.title: WEEK 2 - FOUNDATION BUILD I
2.coachNote: Progress only when Week 1 technique was clean. Rest 60-90 sec between circuit rounds. Track-first adjustment: Complete high-intensity sprint work before lifting. If the athlete is unusually fatigued, remove the final circuit round or accessory block before reducing the quality of the primary sprint session.

3.title: WEEK 3 - FOUNDATION BUILD II
3.coachNote: Highest-stress week of Wave 1. Stop Olympic sets if speed or technique clearly deteriorates. Track-first adjustment: Complete high-intensity sprint work before lifting. If the athlete is unusually fatigued, remove the final circuit round or accessory block before reducing the quality of the primary sprint session.

4.title: WEEK 4 - DELOAD / CONSOLIDATE
4.coachNote: Deload: cut volume, keep movement quality. No need to chase fatigue. Track-first adjustment: Complete high-intensity sprint work before lifting. If the athlete is unusually fatigued, remove the final circuit round or accessory block before reducing the quality of the primary sprint session.

5.title: WEEK 5 - FOUNDATION BUILD III
5.coachNote: Return from deload with controlled volume. Rest 60-90 sec between circuit rounds. Track-first adjustment: Complete high-intensity sprint work before lifting. If the athlete is unusually fatigued, remove the final circuit round or accessory block before reducing the quality of the primary sprint session.

6.title: WEEK 6 - FOUNDATION STRENGTH
6.coachNote: Main lifts become more strength-oriented; explosive lifts remain fast. Track-first adjustment: Complete high-intensity sprint work before lifting. If the athlete is unusually fatigued, remove the final circuit round or accessory block before reducing the quality of the primary sprint session.

7.title: WEEK 7 - FOUNDATION STRENGTH PEAK
7.coachNote: Heaviest foundation week, not a max-out. No missed reps and no grinders. Track-first adjustment: Complete high-intensity sprint work before lifting. If the athlete is unusually fatigued, remove the final circuit round or accessory block before reducing the quality of the primary sprint session.

8.title: WEEK 8 - FOUNDATION TRANSITION

sections.title: FRI - Optional Neural Primer
entries: Programming note: The exercise families were selected from the surviving original Coach Williams lifting sheet. The eight-week
loading progression is a newly constructed progression designed to support the current MW Sprint Performance System; it is not
represented as a reconstruction of missing historical weeks.
Strength & Speed Development -> Power -> Competition -> Peak
Continuation of the approved Weeks 1-8 Foundation format. Every session is self-contained: exercises, sets, reps, loading and
support work are written directly into the weekly prescription.
Loading: percentages refer to a technically reliable training max for that specific lift. Olympic-lift percentages are based on the
Olympic lift/variation itself. Athletes without a safe, technically sound max should use coach-selected loads that preserve the
Rest: 2-3 minutes for primary strength and explosive work; about 20-30 seconds between support-circuit exercises as needed and
Track-first rule: high-intensity sprinting comes before lifting. When track stress rises, remove accessory volume and optional lifting
Phase objective: Build maximal-strength qualities while preserving explosive intent.

8.coachNote: Finish fast and fresh. Friday is optional if track intensity or competition demands recovery. Track-first adjustment: Complete high-intensity sprint work before lifting. If the athlete is unusually fatigued, remove the final circuit round or accessory block before reducing the quality of the primary sprint session. 41.title: WEEK 41

sections.title: REST OF WEEK
entries: No additional lifting unless specifically prescribed by Coach
Sprint quality, recovery, sleep, hydration, competition readiness
Weeks 25-33 maintain the qualities needed for competition with less volume. Weeks 34-41 taper the weight room so strength and
power are preserved without masking sprint performance with fatigue.
Programming provenance: The exercise families and overall lifting DNA were derived from Coach Williams' surviving original lifting
sheet. Because the later historical sheets are unavailable, Weeks 9-41 are newly constructed prescriptions designed to synchronize
with the current 41-week MW Sprint Performance System; they are not represented as recovered historical workouts.

41.coachNote: Championship week: do not chase fitness. The work is already done. Use only a brief primer if it reliably makes the athlete feel better. Readiness adjustment: If sprint times, mechanics, sleep, soreness or meet demands indicate excessive fatigue, reduce the final support block first. Do not add missed lifting volume later in the week. 41-WEEK WEIGHT-ROOM PROGRESSION COMPLETE Weeks 1-8 establish the foundation. Weeks 9-16 build strength while retaining explosive intent. Weeks 17-24 shift toward power.
